world.bio: I'm a board-certified music therapist (MT-BC) based in Toronto. For nine years I worked in a children's hospital's developmental unit, mostly with autistic kids aged 4-12. This fall I left that job to open a small private practice in a rented room above a bookshop on Queen Street East in Leslieville. I play guitar, keyboard, hand drums, and sing.
skills_assets: MT-BC credential and a Master's in Music Therapy (Wilfrid Laurier)
Nine years of clinical experience with autistic children, hospital referral relationships
A rented 14 x 11 ft room in Leslieville with good natural light and a decent door seal for sound
Guitar, a 61-key keyboard, Orff instruments, a set of hand drums, a gathering drum
A small client waitlist of 11 families from my hospital days
Speaks English, some French; a bit of Igbo from my dad

projects.name: Leslieville practice launch
projects.text: Opening 1 October with 4 clients. The room has a good floor and a window. I still need curtains, a rug, a small cabinet. I budgeted $3,800 for moving, deposits, insurance and furniture, and I did not budget for a piano because a real one seemed impossible. My sessions work best with an acoustic piano: the resonance and the way the child can feel the vibration through the soundboard matter. I keep telling myself the keyboard will do.

projects.name: Parent group pilot
projects.text: A Saturday morning group for parents of newly diagnosed kids, singing and talking. I want to run it monthly, free for the first three sessions. Waiting to see if the room can handle it.

notes.text: Handed in my resignation letter last month, last day at the hospital was Friday. Everyone gave me a card and a mug. I sat in my car in the parking lot and cried for ten minutes. Nine years of kids. I'm both free and terrified.

Went to see the room again. Landlord says I can paint the walls pale green if I put the deposit down by the 20th. The floor creaks at the corner, but that might be good for the rhythm exercises. Stood in the middle and played a G chord. The room answered back. I almost cried again.

Called three piano dealers. A decent used upright is $3,000 to $4,500 plus $400 to move. My whole budget is $3,800 including everything. Someone on a forum said to wait for free pianos on Facebook Marketplace. I've been refreshing it twice a day.

Date night with Daniel. Third date. He asked what music therapy actually is and I tried to explain without sounding like a pamphlet. He said 'so you're a doctor of songs' and I laughed so hard I knocked over my wine. After a long relationship ended I didn't expect to like someone this soon. Slowly.

Balcony tomatoes are dying. First frost warning for next week. Picked the last green ones and put them in a paper bag with a banana. Zinnia seeds saved for next year. Something about saving seeds feels hopeful.

Wrote the liability paperwork for the practice. Insurance is $1,100 a year. Had a mini panic about finances at 2 am. Opened a spreadsheet at 2:15 and it said I can survive about five months at 4 clients a week. If I get to 10 clients, I'm okay. If not, I'm back to hospital contracts.

Ran a free intro session for a mum and her 6-year-old, Leo, who doesn't speak much. He sat at my keyboard and played a single note over and over, then smiled when I matched it on the guitar. That's the moment. I forget why I'm anxious when I'm in the work.
Opening day. Four kids came and one family brought flowers. Leo's mum asked if I had a real piano, because he plays one at his grandma's. I said 'not yet'. I wonder if I should have said 'soon'.

messages.text: Mum: Did you hand in the keys? Me: Yes. Mum: You sure about this? Me: Mum. Mum: I'm just asking. Me: I know. I'm sure. Mum: Then I'm proud of you.
Daniel: Dinner Friday? Me: Yes. I can do 7:30. Daniel: There's a Thai place near your room. Me: Perfect. Daniel: Bring your guitar. Me: Not on a date. Daniel: Fine, but I'll ask for a song.
Priya: Do you miss us? Me: Honestly, yes. Priya: We miss you more. Me: I miss the OT room. Priya: The new hire lost the Orff mallets. Me: Of course she did.
Mr. Kowalski: Rug is fine, just no nails in the wall. Me: Understood. Mr. Kowalski: Sound isn't an issue upstairs? Me: It shouldn't be, I've put felt under the drums.

relations.about: New partner, a high school teacher, tactful and funny
Six-year-old client, non-speaking, plays one note over and over with a smile

constraints: Practice budget is only $3,800 for setup

Won't take clients without a clear safety plan
Needs to keep the rent below $1,200/month
sensitive: Financial anxiety, only five months of runway at 4 clients a week
Sometimes wonders whether leaving a steady job was reckless
